newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia still leading Helsinki to solid gains.
newsitem.headline: Nokia still leading Helsinki to solid gains.

text.p: Shares managed another solid rise on Thursday, with brokers upbeat as Nokia probed ever-higher ground in the run-up to its Q2 report next week.

The FOX portfolio index added 0.71 percent to a new life-high close of 1,239.75, though it was off its session best. The all-share HEX added 0.84 percent to a record closing high 3,617.43. Advancers beat decliners 51 to 29.

After a hesitant patch around midsession, volume picked up as New York took an early shine to U.S. GDP data and Nokia, which opened with a spring in its step and grazed a session high of 475.00 markka, ended up 7.00 at 474.50 -- another best close.
Nokia gained ground amid sustained bullish word from analysts, with JP Morgan upgrading its Q2 forecasts and Lehman Brothers restating an "outperform" stance in a pre-results note.
A Reuters poll this week had Nokia Q2 earnings expectations at 1.64 billion markka in a 1.51-1.85 billion range: Morgan's revised 1.67 billion forecast brought it nearer that consensus.
Brokers showed mounting confidence ahead of the report: "Our star cannot let us down," said one.
Raisio took an early hit on news Monsanto plans a cholesterol-cutting oil, which could rival its patented Benecol agent, but largely recovered to end at 603.00, down 4.00.
Raisio said the plan may not be a threat to its stanol ester, a fat-soluble molecule it adapted from pine residues and which Johnson&Johnson plans to market in the U.S.
One broker cited a view that the global market for foods to cut cholesterol was likely to be large enough for many.
Kone, recently firm amid talk of analysts' favour, put in another spurt when Merrill Lynch confirmed it had started cover with a "buy". The share ended up 20.00 markka at 675.00.
Enso was helped by renewed speculation it may seal a deal on Dutch KNP BT's Leykam paper unit, adding 1.20 markka to 49.70.
